mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Citan 108-112 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM607 engine for the Citan 108-112 CDI costs £1,200-£3,200 supply-only, depending on variant and power output. Supply-and-fit adds £300-£600 labour. Prices vary by variant, engine code, and specialist location across the UK network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes Citan 108-112 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the OM607 engine. The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack and guide wear. If ignored, it can lead to catastrophic engine failure and significant commercial downtime.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR cooler failure on a Mercedes Citan 108-112 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: White smoke from the exhaust, coolant loss, and overheating are the classic warning signs on the OM607 engine. The EGR cooler can crack internally (documented Mercedes TSB fault), allowing coolant to enter the exhaust stream.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes Citan 108-112 CDI OM607 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM607 is fundamentally a robust and reliable commercial diesel engine - 150,000+ mile examples are common. However, it has predictable weak points: timing chain stretch from approximately 60,000 miles, EGR cooler cracking (TSB documented), and turbo actuator failure. All are manageable with the right maintenance schedule and proactive attention.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes Citan 108-112 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM607 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. Timing chain issues typically appear between 60,000-100,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes Citan 108-112 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the Citan is otherwise in good condition with no structural rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM607 costs £1,200-£3,200 - far less than replacing a £3,000-£10,000 vehicle. Commercial operators typically save £10,000+ versus purchasing a new Citan van.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Citan 108/109/110/111/112 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes-Benz Citan W415 launched in 2012 as a rebadged variant of the Renault Kangoo, powered by the Renault-sourced OM607 1.5-litre diesel engine. This engine family, known as the K9K dCi in Renault terminology, formed the backbone of the Citan diesel range across five power outputs: 75hp (108 CDI), 90hp (109 CDI), 95hp (110 CDI), and 110hp (111 CDI), with the 112 CDI representing a later 116hp variant. Over 85% of Citan engine replacement searches target this engine code, making it the most common replacement query for the model. Production continued through to 2021 when the W420 generation introduced updated OM608 engines.

OM607.951 (K9K608), 1.5L four-cylinder diesel, 90hp (109 CDI, W415 launch)

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Citan 108/109/110/111/112 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The OM607 1.5-litre diesel is the commercial backbone of the W415 Citan range - a robust and efficient engine capable of 150,000+ miles with proper maintenance. However, its most common failure points can be catastrophic if ignored. The single most critical issue is timing chain stretch from approximately 60,000 miles, followed by EGR cooler cracking (a documented Mercedes TSB fault) and turbo actuator failure. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM607 Timing Chain Stretch - The Most Critical Citan Diesel Failure
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Citan 108 CDI, 109 CDI, 110 CDI, 111 CDI, 112 CDI (OM607.951, 2012-2021)
problems.rootCause: The OM607 diesel engine uses a timing chain tensioner design that gradually loses hydraulic pressure, allowing the timing chain to stretch and slacken. A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign. If ignored, the chain can jump timing or snap, causing piston-to-valve contact and complete engine destruction. This is the single most common high-mileage failure in the Citan diesel range.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full timing chain kit replacement: chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000+ miles. Recommended for high-mileage OM607s as preventative maintenance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM607 engine with upgraded timing components, new EGR cooler, full gasket set
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain failure caused valve or piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2012-2021 Citan 108-112 CDI is worth approximately £3,000-£10,000 depending on generation, mileage and condition. A rebuilt OM607 engine costing £1,600-£3,200 typically extends vehicle life by 80,000-120,000 miles, making replacement significantly more economical than purchasing a new or used replacement van.
problems.recommendation: If you catch the chain rattle early on cold starts - before any running issues or warning lights - a preventative timing chain replacement at an independent specialist makes financial sense on a Citan valued at £3,000-£10,000. However, if the engine has already jumped timing or snapped the chain, replacement is almost always the better value than attempting a full rebuild of a damaged engine. Independent specialists typically charge 30-40% less than main dealers for chain replacement work.

problems.h4: OM607 EGR Cooler Failure - The White Smoke & Overheating Fault
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Citan 108 CDI, 109 CDI, 110 CDI, 111 CDI, 112 CDI (OM607.951, 2012-2021)
problems.rootCause: The original EGR cooler casting develops hairline cracks internally, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust stream. This produces thick white smoke from the exhaust and can lead to coolant loss, overheating, and eventual head gasket failure if left unaddressed. Mercedes issued a TSB acknowledging the fault across the OM607 family.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of cracked EGR cooler with revised/updated unit. Coolant flush and refill
repairOptions.longevity: Permanently resolves the white smoke issue when using updated cooler castings

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM607 engine including updated EGR cooler and full gasket set
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if cooler failure caused overheating and engine warping

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical Citan 108-112 CDI is worth £3,000-£10,000.
problems.recommendation: The EGR cooler failure is one of the most common Citan diesel faults, but it's rarely a reason to replace the whole engine - unless the owner ignored the symptoms for months and caused overheating damage. Replacing just the EGR cooler at an independent specialist (using a revised post-TSB unit) typically costs under £750 and solves the problem permanently. If you've already seen the temperature gauge climb or lost significant coolant, have a compression test done before deciding on replacement versus repair.

problems.group: OM607 Turbo Actuator & DPF Pressure Sensor Failure
problems.h4: OM607 Turbo Actuator & DPF Pressure Sensor Failure - Loss of Power & Emissions Issues
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Citan 108 CDI, 109 CDI, 110 CDI, 111 CDI, 112 CDI (OM607.951, 2012-2021)
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger actuator can fail or stick, causing loss of boost and reduced power. The exhaust back pressure sensor can fail or become contaminated, sending incorrect readings to the ECU and preventing proper DPF regeneration. This leads to frequent regen attempts, black smoke on acceleration, loss of engine power, and a strong exhaust smell.

repairOptions.longevity: Resolves DPF regeneration issues if caught before DPF clogging

repairOptions.longevity: Extends DPF life; replacement required if cleaning fails

repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if engine damage occurred from long-term neglect

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical Citan 108-112 CDI is worth £3,000-£10,000.
problems.recommendation: The exhaust back pressure sensor is a relatively cheap and quick fix (£150-£250 at an independent) and should be your first port of call if you're experiencing DPF-related warnings or frequent regens. Don't jump straight to DPF cleaning or replacement without having the sensor checked first. If your Citan is used primarily for short urban journeys, occasional longer motorway runs can help maintain DPF health.
